text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Zimbabwe's economy is set to grow by 4.9 percent in 1997 and by at least five percent thereafter, Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe governor Leonard Tsumba said.

- The Zimbabwe government will sell farms to people presently leasing them under the tenant resettlement scheme. But sources say this had raised eyebrows as most of the beneficiaries would be senior politicians and civil servants who originally obtained most of the leases after they were taken from their previous white holders.

- Daggers are drawn at Zimbabwe's immigration department in a wrangle pitting the chief immigration officer against his deputy. The latter alleges he was victimised for uncovering what he called rampant corruption in the department.

- The Airforce of Zimbabwe has deployed its two helicopter squadrons to assist with the evacuation of flood victims and the airlifting of relief food to people marooned in the southern African country and neighbouring Mozambique.
- President Robert Mugabe will on Friday afternoon lay the foundation stone for Zimbabwe's new Harare International Airport.
- More than 1,000 applicants for Zimbabwe's national army training programme turned violent on Thursday after being told their applications had been unsuccessful. Fifty have so far been arrested.
